overview: Each Senate committee needs approval for its operating budget, and this resolution, written by the Committee on the Budget, requests that budget for March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2027. That committee writes the yearly congressional budget plan that sets overall spending and revenue targets. It would cap the committee's spending at $4,630,478 for March through September 2025, $7,937,962 for the fiscal year running October 2025 through September 2026, and $3,307,484 for October 2026 through February 2027, paid from the Senate's contingent fund, with smaller limits on spending for outside consultants and staff training. It also allows the committee to hire staff and, with approval, use staff from federal agencies. On February 13, 2025, it was referred to the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, which reviews committee budgets; the Senate later approved overall committee funding in a separate combined resolution (S. Res. 94).
for: Supporters say the committee needs dependable staff and funding to draft the annual budget plan and analyze federal spending and revenue.
against: Critics say committee budget requests deserve close review as spending on Congress itself, and the amounts are set with little public debate.
